subject: RE: [BULK] Re: Encord <> Jenoptik | Demo Debrief
text:
Hi Charlotte,

Thanks for setting up the next meeting. Here are the questions with the answers you were able to give:

1. Would Encord require a certain file structure, and in your experience how long does it take to set up your pipeline (e.g. move stuff to buckets / set up file structures etc.)?
                        In the past has taken a few days - few weeks. Previous clients have been using fiftyone and other tools like Jenoptik uses, and have moved to Encord in the past very easily.

2. On your website it says there is an option to run on private cloud, would that mean Jenoptik's servers?
Yes, vpc is in the highest price bracket only, so that could cause a potential issue. However, in order to not hike up the price we might be able to come to some arrangement. The previous discussion also mentioned that previous Encord clients have had similar requests regarding data storage location, and it is possible to ensure that data never leaves UK/Europe.

3. How many people can use the Encord tools at the same time / does that impact cost?
No limit on the number of users, but team size would be factored into the pricing. In addition there are standard frames and gpu-accelerated frames. Since we are able to provide our own embeddings, gpu-accelerated frames would not be needed, unless we wanted to use other models such as CLIP for data exploration via text prompts, or SAM for annotation tasks. Gpu-accelerated frames have a cost in the order of magnitude of 2x.

4. Encord does not get involved in any training procedures, such as hyperparameter search/tuning. Does this mean there is no capacity to reproduce mlflow / weights&biases style visualisations (e.g. a very basic use case: loss curves to see if models have converged)?
Clients often run Encord tools side by side with weights and biases, but there is no capacity to have these visualisations within Encord tools themselves. However model performance can be computed, and can be computed on any number of test slices.

subject: Re: Ambi <> Encord
text:
Hi Jamie,

Following up with some answers to your questions:

*Platform*

   - Expected number of users to be registered with the Encord platform
   (i.e. admins, ML engineers and annotators)

5-10

   - Expected volumes of data (i.e. number of images, videos w/ average
   length) to go through the Encord platform over the next twelve months.

As I mentioned, our #1 priority is the annotation service and we would look
into the platform only after. That being said, to give some context we have
over 1B images collected over the past 3 years. Unsure if we will migrate
all/some of those into the platform, but it gives you a sense of our yearly
data collection volume.

*Annotation Services*

   - Expected amount of images/frames to be annotated per month/year?

So our volume was a bit lower last year as it was mainly sustaining
engineering of older models - somewhere in the ballpark of 50-60k images.
That being said, a decent chunk of this was "dense" annotations where there
are numerous annotations per image. See tasks below.

This year could be much higher as we look to support next-gen models such
as PRIME-1. That being said, we are still scoping out the next steps on
that front and thus can't concretely say which tasks we will pursue / what
annotations will be required.

   - Task(s) description

The best way to break this down is we have object-centric annotation tasks
and then sparse/dense annotation of individual images.

Tasks:

   - Classification: Classify the object or some properties about it
   - Segmentation: Segment the object

Note that these are often combined - i.e. segment then classify each
segmented polygon.

Sparse/dense:

   - Sparse: You're doing this for 1-3 objects/image
   - Dense: You're doing this for 10-20 objects/image

 Hope this helps. Looking forward to chatting tmrw!

Best,
Vishal

subject: Re: Labeler Feedback
text:
Hi Anurag,

Do you see the Active access for annotators changing any time soon? Or any way to meet our objective and address these complaints? I understand the role definitions but these limitations severely impact our labeling process. This has gotten to the point where we have had labelers request that we upload our data to a different free labeling service so that they are able to label how they would like. 

The main complaints from external labelers seem to be that they are not able to quickly review their data that they have already labeled and quickly revisit it for relabeling as requested. We had also voiced similar concerns when we were internally labeling with our engineers but have been able to work through some of these pains by using Active. 

As you could understand, we don't want our outside labelers having Admin access. However, if we can't efficiently start using external labelers, our business will start being affected. We are just starting to use external labelers, so I would assume there are some growing pains in getting the best process to work. 

Best,

Hi Diarmuid, 

Thank you for your response, I will pass these tips on to our annotators. 

I have created a labeler account from my personal email and am running into a few different issues that make the labeling process very cumbersome. I gave my labeler account access to only Annotate.

- Once a task is submitted, labelers are not able to look back or correct any labels which ends up causing a heavier management burden for our engineers. If we want to request a relabel from our labelers, it is difficult to reassign them the whole project without having to go through the formal "Review" process or reassign them images with "Reopen". I attached a screenshot from my labeler account after I accidentally hit "Submit" in the top right corner after labeling the first image in the sequence. When I tried to get back to labeling, the system would not let me without an admin account interfering. 

- Since I want to give better reviewing power to our labelers, I would like to give them access to Active. I gave my labeler account "Annotate" access without "Review" because it has confused our labelers in the past and the Review pipeline is generally too slow for them to efficiently use. It seems like I am not able to only provide "Annotate" access with the "Active" access. I have also provided a screenshot from what my labeler account sees of the Active page. 

I am happy to hop on a call if the context above is not enough! I am in PST and am free the rest of the day today. I am also free Thursday morning before 10am or Friday morning before 12pm.
